Marissa — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers below (happy to jump on a short follow-up if useful):

- PO vs card: Our standard is to use corporate card for pilots <$10k and up to 90 days. Anything expected to run longer or >$10k/yr usually goes on a PO/contract. For platform deals we typically request a PO.
- Marketplace: We use AWS Marketplace for ISV billing when possible — that’s preferred by finance for ease of procurement. We are open to listing there but need to understand contract flow.
- Budget owner / finance sponsor: Lisa Park (Finance Director) is the budget owner for platform tooling. Lisa is cc’d.
- Signatory: Final signatory for contracts >$50k is our CFO, Michael Turner (m.turner@acme.com). Contracts team will review.
- Timeline: If we go PO route and everything is standard, procurement estimates ~2–3 weeks to issue PO after SOW/pricing are accepted.

I’ve attached a generic PO template we use internally (PO_template_acme.pdf) — I can share with your ops team if helpful.

Tom

- If ACME wants platform contract or expects >$10k/yr: prepare PO-based offering. We should offer both options in the procurement packet.
- Marketplace option: if they prefer AWS Marketplace, we can support listing but need ~2–3 weeks for partner enablement + legal signoff. Advantage: simplifies billing for Acme; downside: limits custom contract terms.

- Economic buyer: Lisa Park (Finance Director) — budget owner.
- Finance sponsor: Procurement team (Lisa will introduce contact).
- Signatory: Michael Turner, CFO (for >$50k).
- Other stakeholders: Platform eng (Tom) for technical ok, Security (if they ask for SOC2 / docs).
